findings.statement: Subtracting the refusal vector (activation addition) bypasses refusal about as well as directional ablation. However, it raises CE loss on harmless data much more, especially on on-distribution completions, so directional ablation is more surgical.
findings.question: q.refusal_direction
findings.quote: These loss metrics suggest that directional ablation is more surgical than activation addition based methods (§I.1).

findings.statement: An adversarial GCG suffix heavily suppresses expression of the refusal direction at the last token, to levels resembling harmless instructions. Random suffixes of the same length do not have this effect.
findings.question: q.refusal_direction
findings.quote: The expression of the refusal direction after appending the adversarial suffix is heavily suppressed, and closely resembles that of harmless instructions.

findings.statement: The chat-model refusal direction is expressed similarly in the corresponding base models, high on harmful and low on harmless prompts. This suggests the representation pre-exists and is repurposed during safety fine-tuning.
findings.question: q.refusal_direction
findings.quote: This suggests that, rather than developing the “refusal direction” from scratch during fine-tuning, this representation exists already in the base model, and is repurposed for refusal during safety fine-tuning.
